per_shot.note: Furnished hall reads rich and warm; star chart, books, lamp, console clear, but radio is cropped at the left edge, bunk/galley off-frame, and the foreground floor carries a row of evenly spaced round orange blobs that read as a lighting artifact.
Fern, radio with glowing dial, desk and patterned rug all read as themselves; dark recessed floor runner gives structure but leaves the floor in front of the furniture murky.
Rug pattern is strong and woven-looking, books colourful on a lit shelf; rug lies paper-flat with no thickness.
Star chart framed and lit, arc lamp pools warmly on wall; kettle at frame edge is dim and the specimen jars on the table are vague.
Galley (kettle, cups, tile splash, towel), bunk with pillow and blanket, pinboard: the most cared-for corner; kettle sits a little dark.
Cool slate walls with teal trim are a distinct mood, but ceiling fixtures mix cold white and warm amber and the right ceiling stays warm, so the palette reads half-applied.
Dust-rose walls and pink-tinted fixtures make a soft distinct room; close to stock DUSK in hue, separated mostly by the pink cast.
Green walls over a wood wainscot is the most distinct and best-dressed palette; floor stays dark olive with the same orange blob row.

top_issues.issue: Repeated round orange light blobs across the foreground floor
top_issues.why: Evenly spaced identical discs read as a rendering artifact rather than light landing from a source, and pull the eye from the furnishings.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tie floor pools to visible sources (lamp, portholes, practicals) with varied size and falloff; fade the foreground floor toward darker value instead.

top_issues.issue: Palettes only partly re-light the room
top_issues.why: Slate keeps warm amber fixtures and warm ceiling on one side while others go cold, so the mood is inconsistent.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drive fixture colour and ceiling tint from the palette for every fixture, keeping the arc lamp as the single warm accent.

top_issues.why: No thickness or contact shadow, so it floats rather than lying woven on the plating.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the rug a thin slab edge, fringe that drops to the floor and a soft contact shadow.

top_issues.issue: Key furnishings sit dim or cropped at play scale
top_issues.why: Radio is cut off at frame edge and the kettle is under-lit, so bought items lose their read in the wide shot.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each furnishing a small local practical or rim so it holds value at play size; check slot framing in the mid shot.

top_issues.issue: Big beige locker ignores the palette
top_issues.why: The same cream cabinet in every palette dominates the right side and weakens the sense of a distinct room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint or trim the locker with palette accent colour while keeping its form.

protect: Every furnishing reads as itself: patterned woven rug, fern in pot, bunk with pillow and blanket, kettle and cups, coloured books, radio with glowing dial, framed star chart
Warm arc lamp pool on wall and floor and porthole dusk glow
Panelled walls, ribs, conduit and a real ceiling with fixtures
Verdant wood wainscot and slate teal trim as palette identities
Suit stays the brightest, most legible thing in frame

per_shot.note: Same rich furnished hall; floor is lighter plating with soft reflective pools instead of blob row, more lived-in, though the foreground reflections smear and the radio is still cropped.
Fern, radio dial, desk and rug read clearly; porthole light spills across lighter floor plates, warmer and more inviting than A.
Rug now has a raised edge and fringe so it sits on the floor as an object; faint green smear at lower left is a stray tint.
Lamp pool on wall and floor reads well, kettle at edge brighter; foreground floor is a little washed by a broad glow around the suit.
Galley and bunk as cared-for as A; kettle catches light properly and reads as copper.
All fixtures go cool white, ceiling and floor turn blue-steel: a coherent cold room with the arc lamp as the one warm accent.
Rose walls with pink-lit floor plates feel like one soft room; still close to DUSK in hue.
Green over wood wainscot, lighter floor shows plating; distinct and good-looking, floor reflections slightly muddy.

top_issues.issue: Foreground floor reflections smear into muddy blurs
top_issues.why: The soft blotches with green and dark streaks read as noise rather than clean light pools, and the lit floor flattens the dark corners the brief asks for.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tighten floor reflections to the real sources, darken the near foreground and room edges so warm pools stand out against shadow.

top_issues.issue: Palettes are close in temperature for DUSK vs DUST ROSE
top_issues.why: Rose reads as a pinker DUSK more than a separate mood.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Push rose toward a softer, lighter value structure or a distinct trim/fabric accent so it is not a tint of stock.

top_issues.issue: Key furnishings dim or cropped at play scale
top_issues.why: Radio is cut off at frame edge; bunk and galley are off-frame in the wide shot so a full room reads less rich than the close-ups.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Check slot framing so the wide view carries more of the bought set, or give each item a local practical.

top_issues.issue: Big beige locker ignores the palette
top_issues.why: The same cream cabinet in every palette dominates the right side.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint or trim the locker with the palette accent colour.

top_issues.issue: Stray green tint patches on the floor
top_issues.why: Unexplained green spill reads as a bug in the warm hall.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Trace it to a source (console screen or fern) and either motivate it or remove it.

Porthole dusk and arc lamp light landing on wall and floor

why: Same furnishings in both; B wins on palette coherence (slate fixtures all cool), a rug that sits on the floor and better-lit kettle, while A's floor has an artifact-like row of identical light blobs. B's lighter floor costs some dark-corner contrast, so the gap is small.
